title: Decomposition by question facets (foundational)
description: Signature original: A complex question is split along its natural facets: what, how, how well, and compared to what. Each facet becomes an independent subquestion that can be searched without waiting on the others. Facet-based splitting works because most research questions are really several smaller questions wearing a trench coat. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Subquestion Generator, 2026-10-21.

title: Dependency ordering of subquestions (foundational)
description: Signature original: Subquestions are topologically ordered so that ones whose answers feed others run first. Independent subquestions are marked parallel-safe and can fan out to multiple workers at once. The ordering is computed from an explicit dependency list, not guessed, so the execution plan is always sound. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).

title: Subquestion answerability check (foundational)
description: Signature original: Each generated subquestion is checked for answerability: it must be specific enough to search and narrow enough to answer from retrievable sources. Vague subquestions are refined with added constraints before they enter the queue. This check keeps the fan-out from producing dozens of unanswerable micro-questions. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).

title: Fan-out control with branching budget (foundational)
description: Signature original: The total number of subquestions is capped by a branching budget derived from available workers and time. When decomposition proposes more subquestions than the budget allows, the lowest-information ones are merged or dropped. Bounded fan-out keeps the investigation parallel without exploding into hundreds of tiny searches. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
proposed = ['q1', 'q2', 'q3', 'q4', 'q5', 'q6']
budget = 4
kept = proposed[:budget]
print('kept:', kept, '| merged/dropped:', proposed[budget:])
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Subquestion Generator, 2026-10-21.

t: Answer recomposition into the parent answer (foundational)
title: Answer recomposition into the parent answer (foundational)
description: Signature original: Subquestion answers are recombined into the parent answer following the dependency order, with each section citing its subquestion. Contradictions between subquestion answers are surfaced explicitly rather than smoothed over. The recomposed answer links back to every subquestion so readers can drill into any part. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
answers = {'q1': 'inverted index: 40ms', 'q2': 'scan: 900ms'}
parent = 'Comparison: ' + '; '.join(f'{k} -> {v}' for k, v in answers.items())
print(parent)
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Subquestion Generator, 2026-10-21.
